# Ruth Abernathy

Chair of the institute data governance board since 2024. A clinical epidemiologist by training; she ran a cohort data access committee elsewhere before joining Corvane, and it shows in how she runs meetings.

## Role

Ruth sets the board agenda, decides which items need a DPIA before discussion, and owns the policy documents the board maintains, including the [[corvane-data-access-policy-2023]]. She asked Ines to lead the drafting of the [[data-access-policy-revision]] at [[data-governance-board-2026-03-05]].

## How We Work Together

Ruth reads every paper and expects the same. She prefers a draft with tracked changes plus a one-page rationale over a presentation. She is careful about conflicts of interest: she recorded Ines's interest in the consortium clause at the start of drafting and agreed that Ines drafts but does not vote on that item. She also maintains the board's conflict-of-interest register, where Ines's industry contacts are declared ([[conflict-of-interest-handling-vendor-contacts]]).

She supports the consortium clause and has said so, but will not take it to a vote with an incomplete DPIA. At [[data-governance-board-2026-09-10]] she was the one who proposed re-tabling rather than conditional adoption.

## Current Threads

- Draft 4 of the policy due to her by 2026-10-29 for the board on 2026-11-12.
- Revised [[data-governance-board-terms-of-reference]] to add a standing data access committee function for consortium requests ([[data-access-committee]]).
- Annual data request statistics ([[data-request-statistics-2025]]) to be presented at the November board.

## Notes For Working With Her

Ruth will move quickly once the conditions she has set are met; she does not add new conditions at the last minute. The three requests from September are therefore the full list for November, and draft 4 should answer them point by point in the cover note. She has also asked that the cover note quote the 2025 request statistics rather than describe the Halo case alone, so that the board sees the clause as an institute need and not one group's need.
